Part_A.title: Preserving Hong Kong's Culinary Heritage: A Student-Led Initiative
Part_A.instructions: Write a proposal of approximately 200 words to your school principal. Pay close attention to the format and tone expected of a formal proposal.
Part_A.situation: Your school is looking for ways to connect students to Hong Kong's cultural heritage. You believe a culinary project, focusing on preserving traditional food-making techniques, would be engaging and educational.
requirements: Outline the proposed project, focusing on preserving a specific Hong Kong food.
Explain the educational benefits of the project for students.
Suggest how the project will involve the school community.
format_guides: Must include a clear Title and Headings.
Maintain a formal and persuasive tone appropriate for addressing the school principal.
Address the Principal formally (e.g., Dear Principal [Name])

Part_B.question: Your school newspaper is launching a new sports section. As the newly appointed sports editor, you have been tasked with writing an introductory article that outlines the section's mission, values, and planned coverage. The principal has emphasized the importance of promoting ethical sportsmanship and responsible reporting. Write an article (approximately 400 words) that introduces the new sports section, detailing its focus on local school sports, highlighting upcoming events, and explaining how it will promote fair play and positive values within the school community. Include specific examples of how the section will cover different sports and address potential controversies.

Your drama club is preparing to stage a production of a play with a complex narrative and challenging themes. The director is concerned about the audience's comprehension and engagement. As the dramaturge for the production, you have been asked to write a programme note (approximately 400 words) that provides context for the play, explores its key themes, and helps the audience understand the director's interpretation. Your note should also address the play's historical context and its relevance to contemporary society. Provide specific examples from the script to support your analysis, and offer insights into the characters' motivations and relationships.

A local community organization is hosting a poetry and song festival focused on the theme of 'Resilience in the Face of Adversity.' You have been invited to present an analysis of two poems or songs (of your choice) that explore this theme. Write your analysis (approximately 400 words), comparing and contrasting how each work uses poetic/lyrical devices (e.g., imagery, metaphor, rhythm, rhyme) to convey the experience of overcoming challenges. Explain how each poem or song resonates with the theme of resilience and connects with a wider audience. Include relevant quotes from the selected works to illustrate your points.

Your school's debate team is preparing for a competition on the topic: 'This house believes that social media companies should be held legally responsible for the content posted by their users.' You have been assigned the task of writing a position paper (approximately 400 words) outlining your team's stance (either for or against the motion). Your paper should present a clear and concise argument, supported by evidence and reasoning. Address potential counter-arguments and explain why your team's position is the most justifiable. Include specific examples of cases or situations to strengthen your argument.

A local NGO is launching a campaign to raise awareness about a social issue that is affecting your community (e.g., poverty, environmental pollution, mental health). You have been asked to write a persuasive letter (approximately 400 words) to a local business owner, urging them to support the campaign through financial donations, volunteer work, or in-kind contributions. In your letter, explain the nature and scope of the social issue, highlight its impact on the community, and demonstrate how the business owner's support can make a meaningful difference. Provide concrete examples of how their contribution will be used and acknowledge any potential benefits to their business.

You are working as an intern at a marketing firm. A new client, a small local bakery, has requested a proposal for a social media marketing strategy. Write a proposal (approximately 400 words) outlining a plan to increase the bakery's online presence and attract new customers. Your proposal should include specific marketing goals (e.g., increased website traffic, follower growth, brand awareness), target audience analysis, proposed content strategy (e.g., types of posts, frequency, platforms), and a basic budget outline. Explain how you will measure the success of the campaign and provide a timeline for implementation.

Write a review (approximately 400 words) of a recent film, television series, or video game that has had a significant impact on popular culture. Analyze the work's key themes, characters, and narrative techniques. Discuss its cultural significance, addressing its strengths and weaknesses. Consider its impact on audiences, its representation of social issues, and its contribution to the evolution of its genre. Provide specific examples from the work to support your analysis, and offer your overall evaluation and recommendation.

A literary magazine is holding a short story competition with the theme 'Unexpected Encounters.' Write a short story (approximately 400 words) that explores this theme. Your story should feature compelling characters, a vivid setting, and a well-developed plot with a clear beginning, middle, and end. Consider how the unexpected encounter transforms the characters or alters the course of their lives. Pay attention to creating a distinctive voice and using descriptive language to engage the reader.
